model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, CET1 retention on risk-weighted-asset growth, preference-share and perpetual-bond distributions and NCI charged in the flow

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E operating income, RMB m: H1 2026 actual 63,108 (interim key data, -4.31% YoY) + H2 2026E ~59,600 (FY2025 H2 actual 126,460 - 65,951 = 60,509, x 0.985: net interest income growing ~3% on lower deposit costs, fee income -7% and trading/investment gains still below FY2025). FY2025 actual 126,460 (-6.74%), FY2024 135,595, FY2023 145,735. Operating income = net interest income + net fee and commission income + other non-interest income (trading, investment-securities and derecognition gains, FX, other).
inputs.share_count_basis: 59,086m A + H ordinary shares (share capital RMB59,086m at RMB1 par, interim key data; weighted average = period-end in the FY2025 EPS note line 9664 and the H1 2026 EPS note line ~4470), unchanged since the March 2023 convertible-bond conversion (54,032m -> 59,086m). One class with identical economic rights, so the per-share value applies to the H share. Held FLAT: basic = diluted EPS (RMB0.58 FY2025, 0.28 H1 2026); the 300m remaining preference shares convert only on a CET1 trigger (5.125%) that has not occurred; SBC-zero. A discounted A+H rights issue or state recapitalisation is the dilution the flat count does not model (bear-case risk, see notes).
inputs.debt_cash_note: Bank: customer deposits (RMB4.19tn at 30 Jun 2026), interbank and central-bank funding and debt securities issued (RMB1.33tn at FY2025, ~20% of liabilities) are operating funding; cash and central-bank balances are liquidity, not surplus. Net debt is zero by construction on the FCFE route and nothing is bridged after the flows. Reported OCF (-204.8bn FY2024, +162.9bn FY2025, +60.9bn H1 2026) is deposit and interbank flow noise and is not used.
inputs.fcf_note: last_fcf is FY2026E FCFE, not reported OCF - capex: net profit attributable to ORDINARY shareholders ~29,000 (PBT ~42,100 = H1 24,213 + H2 ~17,900 at a ~30% H2 margin given elevated provisioning; FY2026E margin 34.3%; less income tax ~21%, NCI ~0.7% and preference/perpetual distributions ~4.3bn, together ~31%) LESS equity retained to hold CET1 at 9.65% on ~3.5% RWA growth (0.0965 x (5,285,000 - 5,106,238) ~= 17,250) = ~11,800. Against this the Bank pays ~10.3bn of ordinary dividends (FY2025 RMB1.75/10 shares = 10,340m; FY2026 interim RMB0.81/10 = 4,786m) - covered, but only because RWA growth is being held at 3-5%.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero: no share-based payment scheme in the FY2021-FY2025 annual reports; basic = diluted EPS; ShareRepurchases 0 in FY2024-25 (kpis). House and street bases coincide, band_position is degenerate (band collapsed).
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate converts CNY (model; the Bank reports in RMB) to HKD (H-share quote): CNYHKD=X 1.1746 at 2026-10-23T16:03Z, Yahoo Finance chart API. Triangulated: USDHKD=X 7.8422 / USDCNY=X 6.6596 = 1.1776 (same source, same day; 0.26% apart). The Shanghai A share (601818.SS) closed at CNY 2.99 = HKD 3.51 on 2026-10-23, a ~34% A/H premium (normal for a Chinese joint-stock bank), so the dual listing is not a parity check. Per-share values are per ordinary share and apply equally to A and H.
inputs.fy0: FY2026E (year ending 2026-12-31, unreported: H1 2026 actual + H2 estimate)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T08:08:08Z HKEX regular close (Friday); valuation dated Saturday 2026-10-24. Price sits at the bottom of the 52-week range.
inputs.cet1_anchor: Consolidated common equity tier-1 ratio 9.67% on RWA RMB5,197,339m at 30 Jun 2026 (net CET1 capital 502,630; interim lines 363-381); 9.69% on 5,106,238m at FY2025; 9.82% on 4,863,120m at FY2024; 9.18% on 4,824,278m at FY2023 (annual lines 718-736). Tier-1 11.69%, CAR 13.35% at H1 2026. Regulatory CET1 floor 5% + 2.5% conservation buffer + D-SIB surcharge (~0.5pt) = ~8.0%, so the buffer is ~1.6pt - similar to 0998.HK (~1.4pt), far better than 2016.HK (~0.6pt). RWA grew 0.8% FY2024, 5.0% FY2025 and 1.8% in H1 2026; the ratio drifted 15bp in 18 months. The third tranche of preference shares (RMB35.1bn, Everbright P3) was redeemed on 11 Feb 2026 and replaced with new AT1 by June (other equity instruments 104,947 at H1 2026 vs 104,906 at FY2025).
inputs.ordinary_equity_anchor: Equity attributable to shareholders 612,512 at 30 Jun 2026 less other equity instruments 104,947 = ordinary equity ~507,565; BVPS RMB8.59 (interim key data; 8.46 at FY2025). At the current_price converted at fx_rate (RMB2.23) the H share trades at ~0.26x BVPS and ~3.9x FY2025 EPS; FY2025 dividend yield ~7.8% before the 10% H-share withholding.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single CNY cost of equity 11.0% in every scenario (risk charged once, through scenario weights, not the discount rate). Built in the flows' own currency: 10-year China Government Bond ~1.8% (ASSUMPTION, not fetched; the 10Y CGB has traded ~1.6-2.0% since 2025) + beta ~1.05 x China ERP ~6.5% = ~8.6%, plus ~2.4pt for risks the index ERP does not price for an H-share minority in this joint-stock bank. Same 11.0% as the sibling 2016.HK (China Zheshang Bank, 2026-10-17) and 0.5pt above 0998.HK (China CITIC Bank, 10.5%): the CET1 buffer (~1.6pt) is CITIC-like, but the H1 2026 asset-quality break (NPL 1.27% -> 1.44%, coverage 174% -> 150% in six months, credit impairment +31%), the July 2026 Caixin-reported ~RMB20bn gap between reported NPLs (50.7bn) and Stage-3 credit-impaired assets (70.7bn) in the FY2025 accounts, net profit -24% in H1 2026, ROE 6.6% annualised, ~20% wholesale funding and dependence on bond-market gains warrant the Zheshang-level premium. Hurdle for entry price is the house 15%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Bank: IFRS 16 right-of-use depreciation and lease-liability interest (lease liabilities RMB9,534m at FY2025, AR line 11273) sit inside operating expenses and so inside the pre-tax margin. lease_cost_pct_path is zero so the charge is not taken twice; nothing is deducted as debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, inside the 'cash_tax_rate' deduction. The margin is calibrated to PROFIT BEFORE TAX (49,687 FY2025, after credit impairment 36,426) and the deduction covers income tax (10,546; 21.2%), profit attributable to non-controlling interests (315; 0.6%) and distributions to other-equity-instrument holders (4,647 = preference dividends 2,807 + perpetual-bond interest 1,840; 9.4%). FY2025 total 31.2% = (49,687 - 34,179) / 49,687, where 34,179 is net profit attributable to ordinary shareholders (AR FY2025 EPS note, lines 9658-9662). H1 2026: (5,375 + 127 + 2,188) / 24,213 = 31.8% (ordinary profit 16,523, interim EPS note). Other equity instruments (104,947) and NCI (2,597) are therefore NOT deducted again in a bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> dcf-methods routing row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker, thrift'. Run as FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, the house precedent for Chinese banks (0998.HK China CITIC Bank 2026-10-12; 2016.HK China Zheshang Bank 2026-10-17; 1658.HK, 0939.HK). First valuation of this ticker; no MEMORY.md entry. Not an owner-FCF DCF: deposits are operating funding, OCF swings from -205bn to +163bn, net debt is zero by construction. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = operating income; ebitda_margin = pre-tax margin (after credit impairment, the real cost of a bank); SBC, D&A, leases and working capital zero; cash_tax_rate = income tax + NCI + preference/perpetual distributions, so EBIT x (1 - rate) = net profit to ORDINARY shareholders; capex = equity retained to hold CET1 at the target on RWA growth (target x RWA_t - prior target x RWA_t-1, as % of revenue, from an FY2026E RWA of RMB5,285bn), so FCF = FCFE = distributable earnings. Terminal-decade RWA growth is set at or near terminal growth so the terminal FCFE is self-consistent. The 18x terminal cap is above the Gordon multiple in every scenario (12.1x base, 12.9x bull, 11.3x bear) and does not bind. KEY FINDINGS: (1) The dividend is currently covered (FY2026E FCFE ~11.8bn vs ~10.3bn ordinary dividends) but only because RWA growth is held at 3-5%; at the FY2017-21 growth rates the bank could not both grow and pay. (2) ROE on ordinary equity is ~6-7% against an 11% cost of equity, so fair value is a fraction of book: base terminal P/B ~0.42x on ~5.9% terminal ROE. The market's 0.26x prices the bear case. (3) The H1 2026 asset-quality break is the swing variable: NPL +17bp and coverage -24pt in six months while management says new-NPL formation met its target, i.e. legacy Stage-3 assets are being recognised (the RMB20bn gap). The base case assumes two years of elevated provisioning (margin 34-35%) then recovery to 37%; the bear case assumes the gap is provisioned through the P&L and CET1 is rebuilt to 10%. DRIVER EVIDENCE: FY2025 annual (operating income -6.74%; NIM 1.40% vs 1.54%; cost-to-income 30.67%; NPL 1.27%; coverage 174.14%; PBT margin 39.3%; attributable profit -6.88%; dividend RMB1.75/10 shares; CET1 9.69%) and H1 2026 interim (operating income -4.31%, NII +3.17%, fees -7.34%, other income roughly halved; NIM 1.42%, +2bp YoY, first rise after five years of compression from 2.29%; credit impairment +31.25%; PBT -21.08%; attributable profit -24.01%; NPL 1.44%; coverage 150.02%; CET1 9.67%; interim dividend RMB0.81/10 shares = 25.6% payout). Management gives no numeric FY2026 guidance ('maintain NIM stabilisation', 'control new NPL formation', capital above SIB requirements). Valuation date is 9.8 months into FY2026, so FY2026E is fy0 (not discounted) and the first discounted flow is FY2027; the FY2025 final dividend (May-Jun 2026) and FY2026 interim belong to fy0 and are not double-counted.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: terminal nominal growth for a sub-cost-of-capital Chinese joint-stock bank (China nominal GDP ~4% less continued NIM drift and capital-constrained RWA growth), bracketed by revenue 3yr CAGR -5.9% and BVPS 4yr CAGR 4.9%; base revenue path runs 1.5% -> 3.0%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr/5yr CAGR 6.0%/5.9% vs revenue -5.9%/-2.4% and EPS -4.7%/-1.0% (>30% apart). Equity growth is retained earnings plus the March 2023 convertible-bond conversion (shares 54,032m -> 59,086m, +9.4%), not operating growth; operating income has fallen for four consecutive years (153,366 FY2021 -> 126,460 FY2025). Equity CAGR is NOT used as the growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are null: a bank's reported FCF (OCF - capex) is deposit-flow noise. The relevant series is net profit to ordinary shareholders: 36,885 (FY2024) -> 34,179 (FY2025), -7.3%; H1 2026 16,523 vs ~22,300, -26%. Attributable net income peaked at 44,807 (FY2022). NIM 2.29% (FY2020) -> 1.40% (FY2025) -> 1.42% (H1 2026). EPS series is the CSV (diluted) basis: 0.61 FY2020, 0.67 FY2022, 0.58 FY2025.

base.growth_rationale: Operating income +1.5% FY2027 then 2.5-3.0%: NIM has stabilised at ~1.42% (H1 2026 +2bp YoY as deposit costs fell 19%), NII grows ~3% on 3-4% balance-sheet growth, fee income flat-to-down (card fees weak, wealth AUM growing), trading/investment gains normalised at the lower H1 2026 run-rate rather than the FY2025 level.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax margin after credit impairment: FY2021 34.5%, FY2022 36.9%, FY2023 34.1%, FY2024 38.0%, FY2025 39.3%, FY2026E ~34.3% (H1 38.4% vs 46.5%; H2 seasonally heavy on provisioning). FY2024-25 margins were flattered by falling impairment while coverage slid from 181% to 174%; the H1 2026 break (coverage 150%, impairment +31%) says that is over. Base holds 34-35% for two years while legacy Stage-3 assets are provisioned, then recovers to 37% (opex ~30% of income, credit cost ~1.0% of loans - the FY2021-23 level) - below the FY2024-25 peak, no NIM recovery.
base.capex_rationale: Equity retained to hold CET1 at 9.65% (current 9.67%, ~1.6pt above the D-SIB floor) on RWA growth of 4.0% for two years, then 3.5, 3.5, 3.0, 3.0, 3.0, 2.5, 2.5, 2.5% from FY2026E RWA RMB5,285bn (FY2025 5,106bn, H1 2026 5,197bn). RWA grew 0.8% FY2024, 5.0% FY2025, 1.8% in H1 2026; total assets +3.0% FY2025, +1.2% H1 2026. Retention / revenue = g x 0.0965 x prior RWA / revenue: 16.4% in FY2027 falling to 10.5%. Terminal RWA ~RMB7,206bn, CET1 capital ~RMB695bn, terminal ordinary ROE ~5.9%, terminal P/B ~0.42x.
base.tax_rationale: Income tax ~21% + NCI ~0.7% + preference/perpetual distributions (~RMB4.3-4.6bn fixed, ~9-10% of FY2026E PBT; the P3 preference redeemed Feb 2026 was replaced by cheaper AT1) = 31%, vs 31.2% actual FY2025 and 31.8% H1 2026. Held flat; the fixed coupon's share falls as PBT grows (ignored, conservative).
base.terminal_note: Gordon on FY2036 FCFE at 11.0% - 2.5% = 12.1x; 18x cap does not bind. Implied terminal P/B ~0.42x on ~5.9% ROE, consistent with (ROE - g)/(CoE - g).
base.narrative: Two years of elevated provisioning as legacy Stage-3 assets are recognised, then a steady sub-par joint-stock bank: NIM ~1.4%, margin 37%, RWA growth 3-4% so CET1 stays at 9.65% without a raise; the ~30% payout stays covered.

bull.growth_rationale: Sector deposit repricing (high-cost deposits rolling through 2026-27) lifts NIM 5-10bp; wealth-management AUM (RMB2.10tn, +8% YTD) and Cloud Fee Payment/transaction-banking fees grow; bond-market gains recover toward the FY2025 level; balance sheet grows 4-5%.
bull.margin_rationale: The H1 2026 NPL rise is a one-off reclassification (as management claims); credit cost falls back to the FY2025 ~0.9% level, cost-to-income holds ~28-29% (H1 2026 27.4%), margin returns to the FY2024-25 range of 38-39% and slightly above on NIM recovery.
bull.capex_rationale: CET1 held at 9.65% on RWA growth of 5.0% for two years then 4.5, 4.5, 4.0, 4.0, 3.5, 3.5, 3.0, 3.0%. Faster growth consumes more capital, which is why the bull value is not proportionally higher than base. Terminal RWA ~RMB7,821bn, terminal ordinary ROE ~7%.
bull.tax_rationale: Fixed AT1 distributions fall to ~8% of a larger PBT; income tax ~21%, NCI ~0.7%.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon 1.03/0.08 = 12.9x FCFE; cap does not bind.
bull.narrative: The NPL spike was a reclassification, not new bad debt: credit cost normalises, NIM recovers a few bp, fees and trading gains grow, margin 40% and the bank grows 4-5% a year on internally generated capital.

bear.growth_rationale: NIM resumes compressing toward 1.3% (further LPR cuts, deposit repricing exhausted), card and other fees keep falling, bond-market gains stay depressed; operating income falls a fifth consecutive year before stabilising at ~2% growth.
bear.margin_rationale: The RMB20bn Stage-3/NPL gap is provisioned through the P&L and coverage is rebuilt from 150% toward 180% while retail and LGFV NPL formation rises: credit cost ~1.4-1.5% of loans for three years (impairment ~40% of a shrinking income, as in FY2020-21 when PBT margin was 26-35% at impairment 36-40% of income), then partial recovery to 32% - below every year since FY2020.
bear.capex_rationale: Regulator and D-SIB pressure after the asset-quality break force CET1 to be rebuilt from 9.65% to 10.0% over FY2027-30 (9.75, 9.85, 9.95, 10.0%) while RWA still grows 3.5, 3.0, 3.0, 2.5, 2.5, 2.5, 2.0, 2.0, 2.0, 2.0%; retention consumes essentially all ordinary profit for two years (FCFE ~0 in FY2027-28, i.e. the dividend is cut or funded by a raise) before recovering. The flat share count understates the damage if the rebuild is done by a discounted rights issue instead. Terminal ordinary ROE ~4.5%.
bear.tax_rationale: Fixed AT1 distributions (~RMB4.3bn) against a smaller PBT (~12-13% of PBT) plus income tax ~20% and NCI.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon 1.02/0.09 = 11.3x FCFE; cap does not bind.
bear.narrative: The Stage-3 gap is real: three years of heavy provisioning, revenue falls again, CET1 must climb to 10%, distributions collapse for two years and the H-share minority funds the balance-sheet repair.

scenario_narratives.base: Two years of elevated provisioning as legacy Stage-3 assets are recognised (margin 34-35%), then recovery to 37%; NIM flat at ~1.4%, operating income grows 1.5-3%, RWA growth held at 3-4% so CET1 stays at 9.65% without a raise. FCFE rises from ~RMB12bn to ~RMB24bn; terminal ROE ~5.9%, terminal P/B ~0.42x.
scenario_narratives.bull: The NPL rise was a reclassification: credit cost normalises to ~0.9%, NIM recovers 5-10bp, fees and trading gains grow, margin 40%, RWA growth 4-5%. FCFE ~RMB14bn rising to ~RMB27bn; terminal ROE ~7%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The RMB20bn Stage-3 gap is provisioned and coverage rebuilt while NIM compresses to ~1.3%; revenue falls again; CET1 is rebuilt to 10% by FY2030, so FCFE is ~0 for FY2027-28. Dividend cut or a discounted rights issue; terminal ROE ~4.5%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 40% (same as 2016.HK, above 0998.HK's 35%): NPL +17bp and coverage -24pt in a single half, credit impairment +31%, net profit -24%, and a publicly reported RMB20bn gap between NPLs and Stage-3 assets that peers do not show - the base case already assumes two years of elevated provisioning, and the bear is the case where that is not enough. Bull 15%: NIM has only just stopped falling, fee income is still declining and the bank is capital-constrained, so upside is capped. Base 45%: management says new-NPL formation met target and NII is growing again, so the FY2026 profit drop is partly legacy recognition plus bond-market noise.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is worth the equity cash flow it can distribute after funding its own capital requirement, discounted at the cost of equity. For China Everbright Bank that flow is net profit to ordinary shareholders (after tax, NCI and preference/perpetual-bond distributions) less the equity retained to hold CET1 at ~9.65% on growing risk-weighted assets. The bank earns ~6-7% on ordinary equity against an 11% cost of equity, so it is fairly worth well under book (base ~0.4x); the H share at 0.26x book, ~3.9x earnings and a ~7.8% dividend yield already discounts most of the bear case, which is why the weighted value sits above the price despite a bear-heavy weighting. The dominant near-term risk is asset quality: whether the H1 2026 NPL and coverage break is a one-off reclassification of legacy Stage-3 assets or the start of a provisioning cycle that forces a capital rebuild. Net debt is zero by construction; deposits are operating funding.
key_risks_to_valuation: Asset quality: NPL 1.44% (from 1.27%) and coverage 150% (from 174%) at H1 2026; a ~RMB20bn gap between reported NPLs and Stage-3 credit-impaired assets in the FY2025 accounts (Caixin, July 2026). If provisioned through the P&L, the bear margin path applies.

Capital: CET1 9.67% vs a ~8.0% D-SIB floor; a regulator-driven rebuild to 10% while RWA grows absorbs all distributable profit for two years. A discounted A+H rights issue or state recapitalisation would dilute H-share value; the flat share count does not model it.

NIM: 2.29% (FY2020) to 1.40% (FY2025); the H1 2026 +2bp stabilisation depends on deposit costs falling faster than loan yields (3.37%, -32bp YoY); further LPR cuts without deposit repricing take the bear revenue path.
Earnings quality: other non-interest income (trading, investment-securities and derecognition gains, ~10% of income) roughly halved in H1 2026 and swings PBT by a fifth; card fees falling.

Governance and transparency: the bad-loan disclosure controversy and a JPMorgan Sell rating (target HKD2.60, July 2026) at a price near the 52-week low; state-directed lending under the 'five target areas' and Everbright Group control (no buyback lever).

Currency and listing: RMB flows against an HKD quote (a 10% RMB move is a 10% move in HKD value); H shares trade at a ~34% discount to the A shares; 10% dividend withholding for H-share holders is not modelled.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (6818.HK, HKD) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 2.585-3.88. FX CNYHKD=X, USDCNY=X, USDHKD=X and the A share 601818.SS from the same API on 2026-10-23.
